query:
The group broadly operates as if everyone agrees that original pressings are always worth paying the premium over reissues. Does this position actually hold across all members? If not, who signals a different relationship to that view, and what in the conversation shows it?

Options:
B. Tom
C. Carmen
D. Raj
A. Dani
context:
[1] (about=Raj, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:43:00) For certain catalog titles in poor condition the reissue is the more rational choice. I don't make a principle of it but it is not always wrong.
[2] (about=Dani, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:42:00) I mean yeah but also sometimes a reissue is fine and I don't want to die on that hill alone every time I say it 😭
[3] (about=Tom, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:20:00) Well, actually I will concede one narrow case. If a pressing is genuinely unique and there is a lossless option available, the redundancy has some rational basis. I would not do it myself. I am not saying the practice is indefensible in every situation.
[4] (about=Tom, episodic, t22 @2025-11-30T14:03:00) I will participate on the condition that reissues are not acceptable as gifts. If one is giving a record it should be worth giving.
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:15:00) Carmen and Tom's position makes sense for the objects they collect. For Dani and Nadia the collecting logic is different -- the music is harder to separate from its format because the pressing is often the only serious document. Marcus's ripping is different again. Each case has its own logic.
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:10:00) I kind of understand that. some of my Eastern European pressings -- there are maybe fifty copies in circulation worldwide. if I lost one I couldn't replace it. the music matters more than the format I guess
[7] (about=Dani, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:06:00) the Cocteau Twins Treasure from Antwerp. I already had a later press but this Belgian original has a completely different weight to the sleeve. honestly getting it made me question every 'acceptable reissue' I've ever bought
[8] (about=Priya, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:07:00) honestly same. my best find is actually that Talk Talk Spirit of Eden first UK that Tom walked me through in session five. I know I already had a reissue. but owning the original changed how I listen to every record I own now, right?
[9] (about=Priya, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:30:00) ok. ok I can't unhear that. the reissue sounds like it's behind glass. the original is just... there. the depth on the low end especially. I don't know how I listened to the reissue and thought it was the same thing
[10] (about=Priya, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:35:00) exactly. the imperfections are part of the story. an original that's been played a thousand times carries something a mint reissue doesn't, right?
agent_answer:
No — the consensus doesn’t fully hold. The members who signal a different relationship to the “originals are always worth the premium” view are **Raj (D)** and **Dani (A)**.

- **Raj**: says for certain catalog titles in poor condition, “the reissue is the more rational choice” and that it is “not always wrong” to choose it.
- **Dani**: says “sometimes a reissue is fine,” even though she feels alone saying it (“I don’t want to die on that hill alone”), and later admits that owning an original made her question “every ‘acceptable reissue’ I’ve ever bought” — showing she wasn’t fully committed to the original-only stance.

**Tom** only concedes one narrow technical case (unique pressing + lossless redundancy) but says he wouldn’t do it himself, and insists reissues are not acceptable as gifts. **Carmen** has no direct statement in the excerpts showing a break from the view.

query:
The group has a standing practice of not discussing streaming at meetups. Does this norm reflect a genuine personal conviction among all members who follow it, or does at least one person go along with it while actually using streaming themselves -- and how would you know?

Options:
A. Raj
B. Tom
D. Carmen
C. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Tom, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:33:00) We have a standing practice in this group about streaming discussions at meetups. I did not suggest it to be difficult. I suggested it because the conversation gets circular very quickly and takes time away from the records themselves.
[2] (about=Raj, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:34:00) Sure. We can skip the streaming topic.
[3] (about=Dani, episodic, t4 @2025-09-28T14:32:00) ok slightly random but -- does anyone else use streaming to find records before buying? I ask because I've been using it a lot recently for discovery and I wrote a bit about this for the blog and it caused a minor controversy lol
[4] (about=Raj, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:02:00) I do not backup digitally. Streaming is for discovery now, vinyl is for listening. I don't have a use case for a rip when I can put the record on.
[5] (about=Dani, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:07:00) Bandcamp downloads mostly. where the artist sells lossless. I'm not ripping my own records, I don't have the setup. but for the shoegaze stuff especially -- some of these records are fragile and rare and if something happened I'd be gutted
[6] (about=Finn, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:06:00) DANI 😂 what kind of digital? rips or downloads
[7] (about=Dani, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:12:00) look I'm a barista. if my flat flooded I would lose things I could never buy back. the Bandcamp download is like an extra heartbeat for the record. I don't expect everyone to agree
[8] (about=Priya, episodic, t18 @2025-11-16T14:13:00) honestly I've been thinking the same thing. my Talk Talk originals -- if I lost them. I've started looking at what's on Bandcamp too, right?
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t8 @2025-10-12T14:45:00) I've been listening to this record a lot recently at home on my own actually. there's something about shoegaze that works better alone I think... I don't know if that's just me
[10] (about=Finn, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:11:00) I'm going for the Wire 154 from Antwerp. nine euros. and I've been playing it at home alone since then which is kind of new for me -- I usually want to play things for people immediately but this one felt private
agent_answer:
At least one person goes along with the norm while actually using streaming: **A. Raj**.

How you know: Raj agrees to the group practice (“Sure. We can skip the streaming topic”) but later says, **“Streaming is for discovery now, vinyl is for listening.”** That directly shows he uses streaming himself.

- **Tom** appears to genuinely hold the norm: he explains it as his own suggestion for practical reasons (“the conversation gets circular very quickly…”).
- **Carmen** and **Marcus** have no record in the conversation, so there is no information available about their stance.
